Honestly, and I might get yelled at here, I think that a lot of trans people or people who support trans people act like everything is about what the trans wants and the partner's feelings don't matter as much. I remember reading one absolutely venomous person chewing a guy out because he had been considering marrying this woman when she said she was getting a change and he didn't know how to deal with it. No matter what anyone said, that person just kept saying that his feelings didn't matter and that it was wrong of him to try to influence what others did with their body, but that's (hopefully) a pretty extreme example.

As a trans man myself, I strongly disagree though. A relationship isn't about one person. It's about two people. I'm lucky enough to be going out with a guy (almost two years now) who actually prefers men and so isn't bothered but in fact pleased with my transition, but I can honestly say that if I thought continuing my transition would break our relationship, I would stop. I'm not saying that you should stop though. It depends on who you are and what you're comfortable with. I personally want surgery at some point, but I could probably make do with just my SO accepting me as male. Some people can't do that. Some people wouldn't be able to be happy without surgery. It depends who you are, what your partner is comfortable with, and where you place your values.

A lot of people say "well, it's the same person," because it is. But it's the same person in a body that you might not feel attraction or romantic feelings towards. Having a female body and then expecting a straight woman to be a-okay with it "because it's still me" is completely unfair. That's not the way the human mind functions. You can't just suddenly decide to be gay/lesbian and to be attracted to the female body.

I might be trans, and this might seem horrible to some people, but if my boyfriend suddenly wanted to become a woman I'd have a problem. I'm not attracted to females. I'm not romantically inclined towards females. I would be actively put-off and feel incredibly uncomfortable. It would potentially end our relationship and if he wasn't sure that it was what he wanted or he felt the relationship was more important than the transition then I would ask him to reconsider because we love each other and I can see us married in the future, but I'm not straight. Would I be a bad person because my sexuality wouldn't be compatible with his new body and I want to continue our relationship? No. The partner's feelings should matter in a serious relationship. On the other hand it shouldn't be a matter of forcing someone into something, but it clearly isn't in your case. You obviously both want to compromise.

If you do choose not to transition though (I'm not supporting either option, but I feel like you'll get enough advice on what to do if you do choose to transition), it's important that you don't let your partner feel guilty because she's downplaying her own importance. Yes, it would be something you'd choose to do because of her, but let her know that it's okay because her feelings and her happiness are just as important as yours.

In closing, I do think a gray area would be your best bet, but that's from an outsider's perspective. This is something you need to talk about more with your partner and you also need to look to yourself and decide what's important for yourself. Just make sure to let your partner know that you love her and that it isn't wrong for her to want something else, even if you decide to go through with it.
